entities.name: Echinococcosis
entities.description: A chronic zoonotic parasitic infection caused by larval metacestodes of tapeworms belonging to the genus Echinococcus (primarily E. granulosus causing cystic echinococcosis and E. multilocularis causing alveolar echinococcosis), characterized by slow-growing visceral hydatid cysts or destructive infiltrative hepatic pseudotumors with prolonged latency.

entities.name: Hepatic Hydatid Cyst
entities.description: Fluid-filled unilocular or multivesicular larval cyst localized primarily within the right lobe of the liver in cystic echinococcosis.

entities.name: Pulmonary Hydatid Cyst
entities.description: Unilocular hydatid cyst located within the lung parenchyma causing respiratory symptoms.

entities.name: Alveolar Hepatic Pseudotumor
entities.description: Aggressive, infiltrative, pseudotumoral hepatic mass caused by Echinococcus multilocularis metacestodes mimicking liver carcinoma.

entities.name: Cerebral Echinococcosis
entities.description: Expanding intracranial metacestode cyst causing elevated intracranial pressure and focal neurological deficits.

entities.name: Osseous Echinococcosis
entities.description: Infiltrative larval bone infection eroding trabecular architecture without a fibrous pericyst.

entities.name: Splenic Hydatid Cyst
entities.description: Fluid-filled metacestode lesion within splenic tissue causing splenomegaly and left hypochondriac pain.

entities.name: Renal Hydatid Cyst
entities.description: Metacestode cyst involving renal parenchyma and collecting system.

entities.name: Cardiac Hydatid Cyst
entities.description: Metacestode cyst localized within myocardium, pericardium, or cardiac septa.

entities.name: Peritoneal Hydatidosis
entities.description: Multiple secondary hydatid cysts studding peritoneal and omental surfaces after cyst rupture.

entities.name: Polycystic Neotropical Echinococcosis
entities.description: Endemic South American infection caused by Echinococcus vogeli forming conglomerate cystic masses.

entities.name: Unicystic Neotropical Echinococcosis
entities.description: Rare neotropical infection caused by Echinococcus oligarthrus forming solitary cysts.

entities.name: Right Upper Quadrant Dullness
entities.description: Persistent, dull aching discomfort in the right upper quadrant from hepatic capsular distension.

entities.name: Extrinsic Biliary Compression
entities.description: Compression of major intra- or extrahepatic bile ducts by expanding hepatic hydatids.

entities.name: Portal Vein Invasion
entities.description: Infiltration and thrombosis of the portal venous system by alveolar echinococcosis.

entities.name: Inferior Vena Cava Compression
entities.description: Extrinsic narrowing or thrombosis of the inferior vena cava by massive liver cysts.

entities.name: Budd-Chiari Syndrome
entities.description: Hepatic venous outflow obstruction caused by invasive alveolar or compressive cystic lesions.

entities.name: Central Ischemic Pseudocavity
entities.description: Large liquefactive necrotic cavity within an alveolar liver mass outgrowing its vascular supply.

entities.name: Secondary Bacterial Cholangitis
entities.description: Superinfection of cyst cavity and biliary ducts by ascending enteric bacteria.

entities.name: Intrathoracic Cyst Rupture
entities.description: Perforation of hepatic or pulmonary cysts into the pleural cavity or bronchial tree.

entities.name: Intraperitoneal Cyst Rupture
entities.description: Free spillage of pressurized hydatid fluid, membranes, and scolices into peritoneal space.

entities.name: Intrabiliary Cyst Rupture
entities.description: Fissuring of hepatic hydatid into biliary tree with passage of parasitic elements.

entities.name: Spinal Cord Compression
entities.description: Epidural extension of vertebral osseous hydatids compressing spinal nerve roots and cord.

entities.name: Orbital Hydatid Cyst
entities.description: Metacestode development within the retrobulbar intraorbital space causing proptosis.

entities.name: Pancreatic Hydatid Cyst
entities.description: Unilocular or multivesicular cyst situated within pancreatic parenchyma.

entities.name: Mediastinal Hydatid Cyst
entities.description: Extra-pulmonary metacestode localized within anterior or posterior mediastinum.

entities.name: Thyroid Hydatid Cyst
entities.description: Metacestode localization in cervical thyroid lobes mimicking solitary nodule.

entities.name: Muscle Hydatid Cyst
entities.description: Intramuscular larval cyst in thigh, psoas, or gluteal compartments.

entities.name: Mesenteric Hydatid Cyst
entities.description: Freely mobile cyst within peritoneal mesentery or omentum.

entities.name: Cutaneous Metastatic Lesion
entities.description: Remote subcutaneous or dermal larval dissemination in advanced alveolar disease.

entities.name: Pulmonary Alveolar Metastases
entities.description: Hematogenous dissemination of E. multilocularis microvesicles to bilateral lungs.

entities.name: Metastatic Brain Nodules
entities.description: Hematogenous secondary cerebral metastases from primary hepatic alveolar echinococcosis.

entities.name: Systemic Anaphylactoid Reactions
entities.description: Recurrent allergic episodes triggered by subclinical leakage of cyst antigens.

entities.name: Hydatid Pneumothorax
entities.description: Tension pneumothorax provoked by acute rupture of subpleural lung hydatids.

entities.name: Biliary Hydatid Obstruction
entities.description: Mechanical ampullary and choledochal occlusion by impacted hydatid daughter cysts.

entities.name: Cachexia and Sarcopenia
entities.description: Profound muscle wasting and constitutional debility in advanced alveolar echinococcosis.

entities.name: Adrenal Hydatid Cyst
entities.description: Primary or secondary metacestode within the adrenal gland parenchyma.

entities.name: Pelvic Hydatid Cyst
entities.description: Metacestode lodged in the pelvic retroperitoneum or pouch of Douglas.

entities.name: Pleural Hydatidosis
entities.description: Chronic proliferative pleural seeding with thick fibrothorax following cyst rupture.

entities.name: Renal Colic with Hydatiduria
entities.description: Excruciating flank colic caused by passage of daughter vesicles through ureters.

entities.name: Diaphragmatic Erosion
entities.description: Transdiaphragmatic extension of hepatic dome hydatid into thoracic cavity.

entities.name: Hydatid Fremitus
entities.description: Vibratory thrill felt on bimanual percussion of a tense hydatid cyst.

entities.name: Hydatidoptysis
entities.description: Expectoration of hydatid fluid containing white grape-skin membranes.

entities.name: Hydatid Vomica
entities.description: Paroxysmal coughing fit expelling massive amounts of hydatid fluid.

entities.name: Anaphylactic Shock Post-Rupture
entities.description: Sudden cardiovascular collapse and angioedema from hydatid fluid release.

entities.name: Grape-Skin Enterorrhagia
entities.description: Passage of white collapsed daughter cyst membranes in feces.

entities.name: Intrabiliary Rupture Triad
entities.description: Symptom triad of biliary colic, jaundice, and urticaria post-rupture.

entities.name: Hydatiduria
entities.description: Macroscopic excretion of grape-like hydatid vesicles in urine.

entities.name: Stony-Hard Hepatomegaly
entities.description: Rigid, rock-hard, irregular liver enlargement on palpation.

entities.name: Smooth Hepatic Bulge
entities.description: Rounded, smooth, firm liver mass palpated under costal margin.

entities.name: Diffuse Urticarial Eruption
entities.description: Acute widespread erythematous wheals and intense pruritus.

entities.name: Facial Angioedema
entities.description: Acute swelling of lips, periorbital tissues, and facial skin.

entities.name: Visible Abdominal Asymmetry
entities.description: Focal protrusion or distortion of the right upper abdominal quadrant.

entities.name: Decreased Breath Sounds
entities.description: Diminished or absent vesicular breath sounds over affected lung base.

entities.name: Tracheal Deviation
entities.description: Shift of trachea away from affected side due to thoracic mass effect.

entities.name: Echinococcal Ascites
entities.description: Peritoneal fluid accumulation manifesting as shifting dullness.

entities.name: Scleral Icterus

entities.name: Splenomegaly on Palpation

entities.name: Caput Medusae
entities.description: Engorged, radiating cutaneous veins around the umbilicus.

entities.name: Lower Extremity Edema
entities.description: Bilateral pitting pedal and pretibial swelling.

entities.name: Palpable Bone Mass
entities.description: Firm, expanding, painless bony swelling over affected osseous site.

entities.name: Proptosis with Chemosis
entities.description: Forward displacement of eyeball with conjunctival edema.

entities.name: Focal Neurological Deficits
entities.description: Hemiparesis, hyperreflexia, or cranial nerve palsies from brain cysts.

entities.name: Papilledema on Fundoscopy
entities.description: Bilateral optic disc edema and blurring of margins.

entities.name: Bronchial Wheezing
entities.description: Localized monophonic expiratory musical sounds over lung field.

entities.name: Dullness to Percussion
entities.description: Dense percussion dullness over affected pulmonary thorax.

entities.name: Right Flank Fullness
entities.description: Firm, ballottable bimanual mass in the right lumbar flank.

entities.name: Localized Pleural Friction
entities.description: Audible leathery grating rub over lower right hemithorax.

entities.name: Abdominal Guarding
entities.description: Involuntary abdominal wall muscular rigidity and peritonitis.

entities.name: Water-Lily Sign
entities.description: Undulating detached endocyst membrane floating on fluid on ultrasound/CT (WHO CE3a).

entities.name: Spoke-Wheel Pattern
entities.description: Multivesicular cyst with radiating internal septa separating daughter cysts (WHO CE2).

entities.name: Honeycomb Pattern
entities.description: Dense multilocular acoustic rosette of internal daughter cysts on POCUS (WHO CE2).

entities.name: Double-Line Wall Sign
entities.description: Two distinct echogenic parallel wall layers representing pericyst and ectocyst (WHO CE1).

entities.name: Snowstorm Sign
entities.description: Shifting hyperechoic internal echoes from hydatid sand during patient movement.

entities.name: Eggshell Calcification
entities.description: Thick, curvilinear, hyperechoic mural calcification with dense acoustic shadowing (WHO CE5).

entities.name: Geographic Microcalcifications
entities.description: Scattered nodular and ring-like microcalcifications in alveolar liver masses.

entities.name: Central Necrotic Cavitation
entities.description: Irregular avascular pseudocavity with ragged borders inside an alveolar mass.

entities.name: Serpentine Sign
entities.description: Twisted, ribbon-like collapsed parasitic membranes on CT or MRI.

entities.name: Cartwheel Pattern
entities.description: Symmetric radial disposition of daughter vesicles within mother cyst.

entities.name: Daughter Cysts Matrix
entities.description: Daughter cysts embedded in hyperechoic partially solid matrix (WHO CE3b).

entities.name: Solid Pseudotumoral Mass
entities.description: Heterogeneous hyperechoic degenerated mass mimicking solid tumor (WHO CE4).

entities.name: Crescent Sign
entities.description: Subcapsular crescent of air between pericyst and ectocyst on chest radiograph.

entities.name: Cumbo Sign
entities.description: Dual air-fluid level producing onion-peel appearance in ruptured lung cysts.

entities.name: Avascular Hepatic Mass
entities.description: Mass showing complete absence of contrast enhancement on dynamic CT/MRI.

entities.name: Biliary Radicle Dilation
entities.description: Upstream intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation on ultrasound and MRCP.

entities.name: Direct Fistula Visualization
entities.description: MRCP or ERCP demonstration of cyst-to-biliary tree communicative tract.

entities.name: FDG Hypermetabolic Halo
entities.description: Perilesional rim of high FDG uptake on PET-CT surrounding inactive necrotic center.

entities.name: Hypointense Rim Sign
entities.description: Low-signal-intensity peripheral fibrous rim on T2-weighted MRI.

entities.name: Multilocular Swiss-Cheese Appearance
entities.description: Cluster of microcystic cavities on T2-MRI resembling Swiss cheese or a sponge.

entities.name: Truncated Vascular Tree
entities.description: Abrupt termination or tapering of hepatic/portal vessels at alveolar lesion border.

entities.name: Microscopic Hydatid Sand
entities.description: Centrifuged cyst fluid showing free protoscolices, hooklets, and calcareous corpuscles.

entities.name: Refractile Hooklets
entities.description: Acid-fast, birefringent, sickle-shaped chitinous rostellar hooklets on stain.

entities.name: Peripheral Blood Eosinophilia
entities.description: Mild-to-moderate elevation in circulating eosinophils (5-15%) on CBC.

entities.name: Eosinophilic Leukemoid Spike
entities.description: Acute surge in peripheral eosinophil fraction (>20-40%) following cyst leakage.

entities.name: Antigen 5 Seropositivity

entities.name: Elevated Gamma-Glutamyl Transferase
entities.description: Serum GGT elevation accompanying alkaline phosphatase in cholestatic pattern.

entities.name: Direct Hyperbilirubinemia
entities.description: Conjugated bilirubin elevation from biliary tree obstruction.

entities.name: Normal Leukocyte Count

entities.name: Polyclonal Hypergammaglobulinemia
entities.description: Non-specific elevation in circulating total serum gamma-globulins and IgG.

entities.name: Elevated Total IgE

entities.name: Negative Protoscolices Count

entities.name: Normal Serum AFP

entities.name: Normal Serum CA19-9

entities.name: Red Fox Contact

entities.name: Contaminated Raw Vegetables

entities.name: Contaminated Drinking Water
entities.description: Ingestion of unboiled surface or well water carrying tapeworm oncospheres.

entities.name: Wild Berry Gathering

entities.name: Home Livestock Slaughter
entities.description: Unregulated home butchery feeding hydatid-infected offal to domestic dogs.

entities.description: Geographic exposure to Alpine endemic zones of Central and Western Europe.

entities.name: Central Asian Endemicity
entities.description: Residence in hyperendemic pastoral steppes of Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, and Uzbekistan.

entities.name: South American Pampas
entities.description: Pastoral livestock exposure across the southern cone of South America.

entities.name: Tibetan Pastoral Communities
entities.description: High-risk population residing on the Qinghai-Tibet plateau with high disease prevalence.

entities.description: Agricultural workers managing sheep, goats, or cattle with guardian canines.

entities.name: Hunters and Trappers
entities.description: Individuals hunting or skinning wild canids and handling animal pelts.

entities.description: Canids harboring adult egg-shedding Echinococcus tapeworms in small intestines.

entities.name: Feral Swine Hosts

relationships.keywords: hepatic cyst, right liver lobe, hydatid liver disease, unilocular cyst
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Echinococcosis manifests as a hepatic hydatid cyst in approximately 70% to 75% of cystic echinococcosis cases, primarily localized to the right hepatic lobe and causing slowly expanding cystic hepatomegaly.

relationships.keywords: pulmonary cyst, lung hydatid, chronic cough, thoracic echinococcosis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Echinococcosis manifests as a pulmonary hydatid cyst in 15% to 20% of cases, commonly developing in lower lung fields and presenting with persistent non-productive cough, dull chest discomfort, and hemoptysis.

relationships.keywords: alveolar echinococcosis, hepatic pseudotumor, invasive liver lesion, Echinococcus multilocularis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Echinococcosis manifests as an alveolar hepatic pseudotumor in over 99% of Echinococcus multilocularis infections, exhibiting continuous destructive infiltrative proliferation into surrounding hepatic parenchyma.

relationships.keywords: cerebral hydatid, intracranial cyst, space occupying lesion, neuro-echinococcosis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Echinococcosis manifests as cerebral echinococcosis in 1% to 3% of cystic cases and 3% to 4% of alveolar metastases, creating expanding intracranial mass lesions that produce intractable headaches, seizures, and focal neurological signs.

relationships.keywords: osseous hydatid, bone echinococcosis, trabecular infiltration, pathologic fracture
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Echinococcosis manifests as osseous echinococcosis in 1% to 4% of cases, wherein metacestodes infiltrate bony cancellous spaces without developing a fibrous pericyst, causing extensive trabecular destruction and pathologic bone fractures.

relationships.keywords: splenic cyst, splenic hydatid, left upper quadrant, visceral cyst
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Echinococcosis manifests as a splenic hydatid cyst either as an isolated primary lesion or following systemic dissemination, leading to left hypochondriac discomfort, splenomegaly, and susceptibility to traumatic rupture.

relationships.keywords: renal hydatid, kidney cyst, hydatiduria, lumbar pain
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Echinococcosis manifests as a renal hydatid cyst in 2% to 4% of cases, primarily arising in the renal cortex and manifesting with dull flank aching, palpable lumbar mass, or frank hydatiduria upon pelvicalyceal erosion.

relationships.keywords: cardiac hydatid, myocardial cyst, pericardial hydatid, conduction block
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Echinococcosis manifests as a cardiac hydatid cyst in 0.5% to 2% of patients, preferentially embedding within the left ventricular myocardium or interventricular septum, risking dysrhythmias, outflow tract obstruction, and catastrophic pericardial rupture.

relationships.keywords: peritoneal hydatidosis, secondary seeding, daughter cysts, peritoneal dissemination
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Echinococcosis manifests as peritoneal hydatidosis following traumatic or spontaneous rupture of hepatic or splenic cysts, leading to widespread intraperitoneal dissemination and maturation of dozens to hundreds of secondary daughter cysts.

relationships.keywords: Echinococcus vogeli, polycystic echinococcosis, neotropical cestode, South America
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Echinococcosis manifests as polycystic neotropical echinococcosis in humid Central and South American regions, caused by Echinococcus vogeli and forming multi-chambered, conglomerate cystic visceral masses.

relationships.keywords: Echinococcus oligarthrus, unicystic echinococcosis, neotropical infection, felid cycle
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Echinococcosis manifests as unicystic neotropical echinococcosis caused by Echinococcus oligarthrus, producing solitary cysts in the liver, orbit, or lungs via exposure to wild and domestic felid definitive hosts.

relationships.keywords: RUQ pain, liver fullness, Glisson capsule stretch, hepatic mass effect
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Echinococcosis manifests as right upper quadrant dullness and fullness due to progressive mass effect and mechanical stretching of Glisson's capsule by slow-growing intrahepatic cysts.

relationships.keywords: biliary compression, ductal obstruction, obstructive cholestasis, mass effect
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Echinococcosis manifests as extrinsic biliary compression when centrally located hepatic cysts compress main bile ducts or the common hepatic duct, resulting in painless obstructive jaundice and pruritus.

relationships.keywords: portal vein infiltration, vascular encasement, portal hypertension, alveolar invasion
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Echinococcosis manifests as portal vein invasion in advanced alveolar echinococcosis, wherein infiltrative metacestode microvesicles penetrate portal venous walls, resulting in presinusoidal portal hypertension, splenomegaly, and esophageal varices.

relationships.keywords: IVC compression, venous obstruction, collateral circulation, pedal edema
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Echinococcosis manifests as inferior vena cava compression when large posterior hepatic segment cysts or invasive alveolar lesions impinge upon the retrohepatic IVC, causing bilateral lower extremity edema and abdominal wall collaterals.

relationships.keywords: Budd-Chiari syndrome, hepatic vein thrombosis, venous outflow obstruction, refractory ascites
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Echinococcosis manifests as Budd-Chiari syndrome secondary to direct mechanical compression or intraluminal invasion of the main hepatic veins by expanding parasitic lesions, precipitating hepatomegaly and intractable ascites.

relationships.keywords: pseudocavity, central liquefaction, ischemic necrosis, alveolar cavity
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Echinococcosis manifests as a central ischemic pseudocavity in alveolar disease, formed when massive microvesicular conglomerates outgrow their blood supply and undergo extensive central avascular necrosis.

relationships.keywords: bacterial cholangitis, cyst superinfection, Charcot triad, biliary sepsis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Echinococcosis manifests as secondary bacterial cholangitis when an intrabiliary communicating cyst becomes colonized by ascending enteric microflora, causing fever, rigors, right upper quadrant pain, and bacteremia.

relationships.keywords: pleural rupture, intrathoracic rupture, hydatidothorax, broncho-biliary fistula
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Echinococcosis manifests as intrathoracic cyst rupture when dome hepatic cysts erode transdiaphragmatically or pulmonary cysts burst into the pleural space, inducing tension pneumothorax, empyema, or broncho-biliary fistulas.

relationships.keywords: intraperitoneal rupture, peritoneal spillage, chemical peritonitis, blunt trauma
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Echinococcosis manifests as intraperitoneal cyst rupture following blunt abdominal trauma or spontaneous thinning of the cyst wall, precipitating acute chemical peritonitis and life-threatening anaphylaxis.

relationships.keywords: intrabiliary rupture, biliary fistula, daughter cyst migration, ductal blockage
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Echinococcosis manifests as intrabiliary cyst rupture in 5% to 10% of hepatic cases, discharging pressurized hydatid sand, daughter vesicles, and fragmented laminated membranes into the common bile duct.

relationships.keywords: spinal cord compression, vertebral hydatid, epidural extension, myelopathy
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Echinococcosis manifests as spinal cord compression when vertebral osseous hydatid disease erodes through vertebral pedicles into the spinal canal, producing progressive paraparesis, sensory ataxia, and bowel/bladder dysfunction.

relationships.keywords: orbital hydatid, retrobulbar cyst, proptosis, vision loss
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Echinococcosis manifests as an orbital hydatid cyst in approximately 1% of cases, typically presenting in children and young adults with painless progressive unilateral proptosis, visual impairment, and diplopia.

relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Echinococcosis exhibits childhood exposure incubation, wherein primary infection is typically acquired during childhood play with infected dogs but remains undiagnosed until middle age.

relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Echinococcosis is ruled out by mural arterial hyperenhancement on dynamic multiphasic CT or MRI, which excludes avascular alveolar echinococcosis and points to hepatocellular carcinoma or angiosarcoma.

relationships.keywords: elevated AFP, alpha-fetoprotein cutoff, hepatocellular carcinoma, negative boundary
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Echinococcosis is ruled out by a markedly elevated AFP level (>400 ng/mL), establishing primary hepatocellular carcinoma rather than an infiltrative echinococcal pseudotumor.

relationships.keywords: elevated CA19-9, carbohydrate antigen 19-9, cholangiocarcinoma, tumor marker
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Echinococcosis is ruled out by a markedly elevated CA19-9 level (>1,000 U/mL), which strongly indicates intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma or pancreatic adenocarcinoma rather than echinococcosis.

relationships.keywords: negative serology, non-reactive ELISA, negative Western blot, exclusion criterion
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Echinococcosis is ruled out by negative anti-Echinococcus serology across multiple sensitive assays (ELISA and Western blot) in an uncalcified, active hepatic cystic lesion.

relationships.keywords: negative Em2, negative Em18, non-reactive alveolar serology, rule out AE

relationships.keywords: anchovy paste pus, chocolate fluid, amoebic aspirate, amoebic liver abscess

relationships.keywords: malodorous pus, foul smelling aspirate, pyogenic abscess, purulent drainage

relationships.keywords: positive Gram stain, intra-cavitary bacteria, bacterial abscess, microbiological exclusion

relationships.keywords: toxic bandemia, neutrophilic left shift, toxic granulation, acute bacterial infection

relationships.keywords: rapid expansion, tumor doubling, aggressive growth, exclusion of echinococcus
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Echinococcosis is ruled out by rapid lesion expansion documented over weeks to months on serial imaging, which contradicts the slow annual growth kinetics (1–5 cm/year) of metacestodes.

relationships.keywords: absent capsule, missing wall, lack of pericyst, ill-defined cavity
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Echinococcosis is ruled out by complete wall absence, wherein a cavitary hepatic lesion displays ragged, non-encapsulated boundaries without a fibrous capsule or hypointense T2-rim.

relationships.keywords: antibiotic response, clinical defervescence, antibacterial cure, bacterial etiology
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Echinococcosis is ruled out by a rapid fever response to antibiotics within 48 to 72 hours accompanied by lesion regression, establishing an antibacterial-sensitive bacterial etiology.

relationships.keywords: absent calcifications, no microcalcifications, non-calcified mass, exclusion of AE
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Echinococcosis is ruled out by the total absence of calcifications on high-resolution non-contrast CT in an advanced infiltrative hepatic mass, ruling out alveolar echinococcosis.

relationships.keywords: zero eosinophils, absent eosinophilia, normal differential, anaphylactoid rule out
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Echinococcosis is ruled out by the complete absence of peripheral eosinophilia (<1%) across serial determinations in the setting of unexplained recurrent anaphylaxis.

relationships.keywords: beaded strictures, multifocal strictures, PSC pattern, cholangiogram
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Echinococcosis is ruled out by multifocal biliary strictures with diffuse beading and pruned ductal branches on MRCP, diagnostic of primary sclerosing cholangitis rather than focal parasitic compression.

relationships.keywords: infantile cavernoma, neonatal portal hypertension, congenital vascular malformation
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Echinococcosis is ruled out by portal cavernoma in infancy, which indicates neonatal umbilical vein catheterization sequelae or congenital vascular malformations rather than echinococcosis.

relationships.keywords: spontaneous gas, air-fluid level, gas-producing organism, unruptured cyst
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Echinococcosis is ruled out by a spontaneous air-fluid level within an unruptured liver cyst without biliary connection or prior intervention, signifying gas-forming bacterial abscess.

relationships.keywords: Entamoeba trophozoites, erythrophagocytosis, stool microscopy, amoebic confirmation
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Echinococcosis is ruled out by microscopic trophozoites in stool showing ingested red blood cells, which establishes acute amoebiasis and accounts for concomitant hepatic lesions.

relationships.keywords: seronegative status, triple negative serology, immunocompetent host, negative rule out
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Echinococcosis is ruled out by seronegative immunocompetent status across three distinct serological platforms in a patient with a multivesicular hepatic mass, pointing to biliary cystadenoma.

relationships.keywords: simple liver cyst, congenital cyst, thin wall, anechoic, non-parasitic
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from a simple hepatic cyst, which exhibits a paper-thin wall (<1 mm), completely anechoic fluid, no internal septa, and negative serology, whereas Echinococcosis exhibits double-contour walls, daughter vesicles, hydatid sand, or calcifications.

relationships.keywords: Entamoeba histolytica, amoebic abscess, anchovy pus, acute fever
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from an amoebic liver abscess, which presents acutely with high spiking fever, right upper quadrant pain, absence of eosinophilia, and anchovy-paste pus, whereas Echinococcosis presents with chronic latency, intact parasitic membranes, and eosinophilia.

relationships.keywords: pyogenic liver abscess, bacterial abscess, septic shock, toxic bandemia, purulent cavity
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from a pyogenic liver abscess, which causes acute septic fevers, marked toxic neutrophilia, rapid cavity liquefaction, and response to antibiotics, whereas uncomplicated Echinococcosis is afebrile, encapsulated, and antibiotic-refractory.

relationships.keywords: hepatocellular carcinoma, HCC, arterial wash-in, venous wash-out, elevated AFP
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from hepatocellular carcinoma, which demonstrates characteristic arterial phase hyperenhancement with venous wash-out, markedly elevated alpha-fetoprotein, and absence of the dense calcific matrix seen in alveolar echinococcosis.

relationships.keywords: cholangiocarcinoma, biliary cancer, CA19-9, rim enhancement, central necrosis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, which displays progressive peripheral rim enhancement on dynamic imaging, elevated serum CA19-9, and absence of pathognomonic geographic microcalcifications and Em2+ seropositivity.

relationships.keywords: biliary cystadenoma, mucinous cyst, internal septa, mural nodules, ovarian stroma
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from biliary cystadenoma, which features irregular internal septations, enhancing mural nodules, ovarian-like stroma on histology, and negative Echinococcus serology without daughter cysts or protoscolices.

relationships.keywords: hepatic hemangioma, cavernous hemangioma, nodular puddling, centripetal fill-in
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from hepatic hemangioma, which demonstrates peripheral nodular discontinuous puddling with progressive centripetal fill-in on dynamic contrast imaging, unlike non-enhancing avascular echinococcal lesions.

relationships.keywords: hepatic metastases, liver mets, target lesions, elevated CEA, primary cancer
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from hepatic metastatic carcinoma, which features multiple ring-enhancing target lesions with central necrosis, elevated tumor markers (CEA, CA19-9), and known primary extrahepatic malignancy.

relationships.keywords: hepatic hematoma, liver hematoma, blunt abdominal trauma, resolving blood
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from a hepatic abscessed hematoma, which presents with an antecedent history of acute abdominal trauma, evolving fluid density on CT, and total absence of parasitic membranes or scolices.

relationships.keywords: polycystic liver, adult polycystic kidney disease, diffuse liver cysts, thin walls
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from polycystic liver disease, which displays diffuse replacement of the liver parenchyma by hundreds of thin-walled non-calcified cysts without internal daughter vesicles, accompanied by polycystic kidneys.

relationships.keywords: choledochal cyst, bile duct dilatation, Todani classification, biliary cyst
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from a congenital choledochal cyst, which presents with direct congenital communication with the bile ducts on cholangiography, lacking an encapsulated parasitic pericyst or hydatid sand.

relationships.keywords: lung abscess, pulmonary abscess, foul sputum, aspiration, necrotic cavity
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from a pulmonary abscess, which presents acutely with high fever, foul-smelling purulent sputum, and thick irregular cavitary margins with fluid levels, whereas unruptured pulmonary hydatids are smooth-walled spherical water-density cysts.

relationships.keywords: pulmonary tuberculosis, TB cavity, acid-fast bacilli, apical infiltrates, night sweats
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from pulmonary tuberculosis, which presents with chronic fever, night sweats, apical cavitary infiltrates, and acid-fast bacilli on sputum smear, whereas pulmonary hydatid cysts are basilar spherical lesions with intact ectocysts.

relationships.keywords: bronchogenic cyst, foregut cyst, subcarinal mass, ciliated epithelium
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from a bronchogenic cyst, which is a benign congenital subcarinal or paratracheal fluid-filled lesion lined by respiratory epithelium without daughter cysts, membranes, or Echinococcus seropositivity.

relationships.keywords: cystic renal cell carcinoma, RCC, hypervascular septa, mural nodule
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from cystic renal cell carcinoma, which features hypervascular enhancing septa, solid mural nodules, and early contrast enhancement on CT, whereas renal hydatids are avascular cystic masses with hydatid sand or calcified walls.

relationships.keywords: splenic epidermoid cyst, congenital splenic cyst, squamous lining, non-parasitic
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from a splenic epidermoid cyst, which is a congenital thin-walled unilocular cyst in young patients with negative serology and squamoid epithelial lining, lacking hydatid pericysts or daughter vesicles.

relationships.keywords: neurocysticercosis, Taenia solium, scolex dot sign, parenchymal ring lesion
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from neurocysticercosis, which causes small (1–2 cm) ring-enhancing parenchymal cysts with a visible eccentric scolex (dot sign), whereas cerebral echinococcosis produces giant (>4–8 cm) unilocular cysts lacking contrast enhancement.

relationships.keywords: cystic astrocytoma, glioma, vasogenic edema, enhancing mural nodule
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from a cystic cerebral astrocytoma, which features an enhancing solid mural nodule and marked surrounding vasogenic edema on MRI, whereas cerebral hydatid cysts are spherical, sharply demarcated, and non-enhancing with minimal edema.
